description: Agent -> server frames the contract must REFUSE. Every case here is a frame a naive Go port emits by accident, and refusing it costs a whole feature: a rejected hello never registers the host, a rejected heartbeat loses the card, a rejected repos frame freezes the git graph. The reader logs and drops the frame; it never closes the connection.

cases.why: A nil Go slice marshals to null, and .default([]) only fills undefined - so the agent that forgot to allocate its capability slice never registers at all.
Same nil trap one level up: a *AgentUpdateAbility left nil marshals to null, and agentUpdateAbilitySchema.default({}) does not cover null - omit the field instead.
An unknown enum MEMBER is fatal where an unknown FIELD is stripped - a newer agent inventing a capability vanishes from the dashboard, which is why update ability shipped as its own object instead.
A nil *Resource marshals to null and takes the ENTIRE heartbeat down with it; a host that cannot measure itself must send an object of nulls, not a null object.
Percentages are 0..100; a per-core sum (400% on a 4-core box) is a unit bug, and storing it would draw a gauge nobody can read.
percent is .int(): a Go float64 CPU reading marshalled straight through (42.5) loses every heartbeat until someone rounds it, and the failure is silent on the agent side.
message is capped at 512 characters (this one is 513): a diagnostic carrying a whole stderr dump would push the payload - and the failure - into every heartbeat.
limit is .positive().default(300), so Go's zero value rejects the whole repos frame - the git graph then stops updating with nothing on screen to say why.
